[Thinking]
**Providing cosmic age estimates**

The user asked a straightforward question about the age of the universe. The current best estimate is around 13.787 ±0.020 billion years, but I need to verify. The latest from Planck in 2018 shows 13.797 ±0.037 billion years. Earlier data from WMAP9 indicated about 13.77 ±0.059 billion years. I’ll round it to approximately 13.8 billion years and mention the uncertainties and measurement methods like the cosmic microwave background and expansion rate. I'd be happy to explain how these measurements are made!
[/Thinking]

The best current estimate is about 13.8 billion years (≈13.8 × 10^9 years).  

More precisely, analyses of the cosmic microwave background combined with the standard ΛCDM cosmological model give an age of roughly 13.77–13.80 billion years, with uncertainties at the few‑hundred‑million‑year level. This value depends on measured parameters (especially the Hubble constant and matter/energy content); differing H0 measurements introduce small shifts but do not change the age by more than a few percent.  

If you want, I can explain how this age is determined (CMB, expansion history, and other independent checks).
